newsitem.title: USA: Humana to buy ChoiceCare for $250 mln.
newsitem.headline: Humana to buy ChoiceCare for $250 mln.

text.p: Managed health care company Humana Inc. said Thursday it had agreed to acquire ChoiceCare Corp., a health maintenance organization in Cincinnati, for $250 million cash.
Humana said it had signed a definitive agreement to buy all outstanding Choicecare common shares for $16.38 each.
The news comes two days after Humana reported its purchase of Physician Corp of America in a deal worth about $400 million.
The two acquisitions will boost Humana's membership to 6.2 million from 4.8 million, and increase its premiums to $8.5 billion annually from $6.8 billion.

In a statement, Humana said it had obtained a $1.5 billion revolving credit facility from Chase Manhattan Bank to help finance the two deals. Humana, based in Louisville, Ky., said it expected to close the ChoiceCare acquisition this fall.
ChoiceCare serves more than 245,000 members. The ChoiceCare Foundation owns 91 percent of its 14.8 million shares; physicians and other employees own the rest, according to a ChoiceCare spokesman.
